-t7_-guj52Y.title: Surat Al-Ankabut Summary
-t7_-guj52Y.one_line: Al-Ankabut teaches how to relate to life's trials: through mujahadah, steady striving that relies on Allah alone, the only constant.
-t7_-guj52Y.summary: He places Al-Ankabut in the cluster from Al-Qasas to As-Sajdah, where each surah addresses a relationship in our lives; this one is our relationship with trials. Life is meant to be full of tests, so expecting ease is like boarding a roller coaster and expecting a gentle ride. The surah's answer is mujahadah, and he reclaims the word: it first appears in this Meccan surah, before any fighting was prescribed, and means exerting effort against difficulty to reach a goal, while the Quran uses qital for war. He walks through the opening examples: tests that expose the truthful, parents who pressure a child away from faith, people who treat human harm as if it were Allah's punishment, fair-weather believers, and the tempting offer to stay put while others carry your sins. The prophets' stories then show striving in different forms: Nuh's endurance over centuries, Ibrahim's preaching and exile, Lut's emigration. Ibrahim's plea for Lut's town shows that those who live alongside falsehood without resisting it share its fate. The spider's web is the central image: anything relied on besides Allah, whether wealth, health, family or country, is fragile. Even land can be lost, which prepared the Prophet for hijrah. He closes with the surah's tips (Quran, prayer, dhikr, gentle argument) and the promise that Allah guides and accompanies those who strive.

outline.heading: Opening
Al-Ankabut in its cluster: our relationship with life's trials
outline.gist: After Al-Qasas dealt with our relationship to people's stories, this surah deals with the tests and calamities that are a normal part of life.

outline.heading: What jihad actually means
outline.gist: Jihad means striving against difficulty toward a goal, and its first Quranic use predates any permission to fight.

outline.heading: No one is left untested; striving benefits the striver
outline.gist: Saying 'we believe' brings tests that separate the truthful from the liars, and whoever strives does so for his own good.

outline.heading: Parents who push a child away from faith
outline.gist: Honour parents always, but do not obey them when they strive to pull you into shirk.

outline.heading: Equating people's harm with Allah's punishment
outline.gist: Some give up when harmed for Allah's sake and only claim to be with the believers when victory comes.

outline.heading: The offer to carry your sins, and the roller coaster of life
outline.gist: Disbelievers offer to carry the believers' sins if they just stay as they are, but life is meant to be full of tests, like a ride you knowingly boarded.

outline.heading: Arabic: the surah's place and the first appearance of jihad in Mecca
outline.gist: He restates in Arabic that the surah is about our relationship with trials, revealed just before the hijrah, and that it is the first to use the word jihad.

outline.heading: Mujahadah versus qital; tests that expose the truthful
outline.gist: The Quran says qital when it means war; mujahadah is a broad pillar of Islam, and no life passes without tests.

outline.heading: Striving is for our sake: justice, removing wrong; the test of parents
outline.gist: Allah needs nothing from our striving; we strive to establish justice and good. Parents' pressure is the first example of a trial to resist while staying dutiful.

outline.heading: Fair-weather faith
outline.gist: Comparing people's harm to Allah's punishment, and joining only when good results come, is not mujahadah.

outline.heading: Striving regardless of results; refusing the comfortable deal
outline.gist: Mujahadah means continuing until the Hour whether outcomes please you or not; leaving evil unchallenged in exchange for comfort is not allowed.

outline.heading: Recitation of the prophets' stories
outline.gist: He recites the passage on Nuh, Ibrahim, Lut, Shuayb and the destroyed nations.

outline.heading: Nuh's striving was endurance; Ibrahim's was preaching
outline.gist: Nuh's example is the sheer length of his effort; Ibrahim called nation after nation, was thrown in the fire and left his people.

outline.heading: Lut emigrates; 'Lut is in it'
outline.gist: Lut's first act is to emigrate to his Lord; when the angels come to destroy Sodom, Ibrahim protests that Lut lives there.

outline.heading: Silent bystanders share the punishment
outline.gist: Lut was spared because he resisted falsehood; whoever lives with evil without resisting it, even if he disapproves, is struck along with its people.

outline.heading: Every head of falsehood seized for its sin
outline.gist: Shuayb's people, Aad, Thamud, Qarun, Pharaoh and Haman were all taken, and those who resisted were saved.

outline.heading: The spider's house: Allah is the only constant
outline.gist: The spider thinks her house is strong but a gust or a running child destroys it; depending on anything besides Allah ends in heartbreak.

outline.heading: Every false support is a web: wealth, status, health, family, country
outline.gist: Any ally taken besides Allah, from an idol to one's health or country, is as fragile as the spider's web, and the sooner we learn this the better.

outline.heading: Even the land can go: the meaning of hijrah
outline.gist: Every surviving prophet emigrated, and the surah came just before the Prophet's hijrah to prepare him and the companions to leave home for good.

outline.heading: Recitation: Quran, prayer and the People of the Book
outline.gist: He recites the passage on reciting the Book, establishing prayer and arguing in the best way.

outline.heading: Tools for striving: Quran, prayer, dhikr, gentle argument
outline.gist: Allah gives practical tips for facing trials: recite the revelation, pray, remember Allah, and debate others in the best manner unless they are oppressors.

outline.heading: When threatened in your faith: Allah's earth is vast
outline.gist: If your religion, morals or dignity are under threat, leave; patience and reliance on Allah matter more than any land.

outline.heading: This life is play; the true life is the Hereafter
outline.gist: He recites the closing verses on the worldly life as amusement and the home of the Hereafter as real life.

outline.heading: Those who strive will be guided to Allah's paths
outline.gist: The Prophet's road to Madinah was the path he was guided to, though he wept leaving Mecca; nothing is constant except Allah and striving for Him, and Allah is with the muhsinin.

outline.heading: Outro

themes.label: Trials, hardship and resilience
themes.note: Trials are the normal shape of life; expecting ease is the error, and the surah is about how we relate to them.

themes.label: Mujahadah: striving as a way of life
themes.note: Jihad means sustained effort against difficulty, independent of results and not limited to fighting.

themes.label: Family: parents, relatives, kinship ties
themes.note: Remain dutiful to parents even when they pressure you to leave the faith, without obeying them in it.

themes.label: Stories of earlier prophets
themes.note: Each prophet models a different form of striving: endurance, preaching, emigration.

themes.label: Commanding good and forbidding wrong (amr bil-ma'ruf)
themes.note: Living beside evil without resisting it means sharing its punishment, as Lut's story shows.

themes.label: Tawakkul: reliance on Allah
themes.note: Everything besides Allah is a spider's web; He is the only constant to depend on.

themes.label: Seerah events and their lessons
themes.note: The surah prepared the Prophet and companions for the pain of leaving Mecca in the hijrah.

themes.label: Seerah events and their lessons
themes.note: The road to Madinah was the path Allah guided the strivers to.

themes.label: Salah: its meaning, etiquette and significance
themes.note: Prayer, Quran and dhikr are the practical supports for enduring trials.

quran.point: The later permission to fight, contrasted with jihad's earlier Meccan meaning of striving
The Quran uses qital when it means warfare
A trial strikes not only the wrongdoers, so bystanders must resist evil

hadith.gist: Leaving Mecca, the Prophet said it was the most beloved land of Allah to him and he would not have left had its people not driven him out

maxims: Nothing is constant in the universe except Allah
Mujahadah means you keep working until the Hour

stories.point: His striving lasted almost a thousand years: endurance itself is mujahadah
Preached to nation after nation, was thrown in the fire and still emigrated

stories.who: Lut and the angels' visit to Ibrahim
stories.point: Lut was spared because he resisted his people's evil; passive bystanders are destroyed with them
Even one's beloved homeland can be lost; only Allah remains

takeaways: Expect trials as the normal shape of life rather than as a sign something is wrong
Keep striving for what is right whether or not you see results
Do not stay silent beside wrongdoing; resist it where you are
Stop leaning on wealth, health, family or country as if they were permanent; depend on Allah
Use Quran, prayer and dhikr as your support, and be willing to move if your faith is threatened

33:4.ar: مَّا جَعَلَ ٱللَّهُ لِرَجُلࣲ مِّن قَلۡبَيۡنِ فِي جَوۡفِهِۦۚ وَمَا جَعَلَ أَزۡوَٰجَكُمُ ٱلَّٰٓـِٔي تُظَٰهِرُونَ مِنۡهُنَّ أُمَّهَٰتِكُمۡۚ وَمَا جَعَلَ أَدۡعِيَآءَكُمۡ أَبۡنَآءَكُمۡۚ ذَٰلِكُمۡ قَوۡلُكُم بِأَفۡوَٰهِكُمۡۖ وَٱللَّهُ يَقُولُ ٱلۡحَقَّ وَهُوَ يَهۡدِي ٱلسَّبِيلَ
33:4.en: Allah hath not assigned unto any man two hearts within his body, nor hath He made your wives whom ye declare (to be your mothers) your mothers, nor hath He made those whom ye claim (to be your sons) your sons. This is but a saying of your mouths. But Allah saith the truth and He showeth the way

33:5.ar: ٱدۡعُوهُمۡ لِأٓبَآئِهِمۡ هُوَ أَقۡسَطُ عِندَ ٱللَّهِۚ فَإِن لَّمۡ تَعۡلَمُوٓاْ ءَابَآءَهُمۡ فَإِخۡوَٰنُكُمۡ فِي ٱلدِّينِ وَمَوَٰلِيكُمۡۚ وَلَيۡسَ عَلَيۡكُمۡ جُنَاحࣱ فِيمَآ أَخۡطَأۡتُم بِهِۦ وَلَٰكِن مَّا تَعَمَّدَتۡ قُلُوبُكُمۡۚ وَكَانَ ٱللَّهُ غَفُورࣰ ا رَّحِيمًا
33:5.en: Proclaim their real parentage. That will be more equitable in the sight of Allah. And if ye know not their fathers, then (they are) your brethren in the faith, and your clients. And there is no sin for you in the mistakes that ye make unintentionally, but what your hearts purpose (that will be a sin for you). Allah is ever Forgiving, Merciful

33:6.ar: ٱلنَّبِيُّ أَوۡلَىٰ بِٱلۡمُؤۡمِنِينَ مِنۡ أَنفُسِهِمۡۖ وَأَزۡوَٰجُهُۥٓ أُمَّهَٰتُهُمۡۗ وَأُوْلُواْ ٱلۡأَرۡحَامِ بَعۡضُهُمۡ أَوۡلَىٰ بِبَعۡضࣲ فِي كِتَٰبِ ٱللَّهِ مِنَ ٱلۡمُؤۡمِنِينَ وَٱلۡمُهَٰجِرِينَ إِلَّآ أَن تَفۡعَلُوٓاْ إِلَىٰٓ أَوۡلِيَآئِكُم مَّعۡرُوفࣰ اۚ كَانَ ذَٰلِكَ فِي ٱلۡكِتَٰبِ مَسۡطُورࣰ ا
33:6.en: The Prophet is closer to the believers than their selves, and his wives are (as) their mothers. And the owners of kinship are closer one to another in the ordinance of Allah than (other) believers and the fugitives (who fled from Mecca), except that ye should do kindness to your friends. This is written in the Book (of nature)

33:12.ar: وَإِذۡ يَقُولُ ٱلۡمُنَٰفِقُونَ وَٱلَّذِينَ فِي قُلُوبِهِم مَّرَضࣱ مَّا وَعَدَنَا ٱللَّهُ وَرَسُولُهُۥٓ إِلَّا غُرُورࣰ ا
33:12.en: And when the hypocrites, and those in whose hearts is a disease, were saying: Allah and His messenger promised us naught but delusion

33:13.ar: وَإِذۡ قَالَت طَّآئِفَةࣱ مِّنۡهُمۡ يَٰٓأَهۡلَ يَثۡرِبَ لَا مُقَامَ لَكُمۡ فَٱرۡجِعُواْۚ وَيَسۡتَـٔۡذِنُ فَرِيقࣱ مِّنۡهُمُ ٱلنَّبِيَّ يَقُولُونَ إِنَّ بُيُوتَنَا عَوۡرَةࣱ وَمَا هِيَ بِعَوۡرَةٍۖ إِن يُرِيدُونَ إِلَّا فِرَارࣰ ا
33:13.en: And when a party of them said: O folk of Yathrib! There is no stand (possible) for you, therefor turn back. And certain of them (even) sought permission of the Prophet, saying: Our homes lie open (to the enemy). And they lay not open. They but wished to flee

33:14.ar: وَلَوۡ دُخِلَتۡ عَلَيۡهِم مِّنۡ أَقۡطَارِهَا ثُمَّ سُئِلُواْ ٱلۡفِتۡنَةَ لَأٓتَوۡهَا وَمَا تَلَبَّثُواْ بِهَآ إِلَّا يَسِيرࣰ ا
33:14.en: If the enemy had entered from all sides and they had been exhorted to treachery, they would have committed it, and would have hesitated thereupon but little

33:15.ar: وَلَقَدۡ كَانُواْ عَٰهَدُواْ ٱللَّهَ مِن قَبۡلُ لَا يُوَلُّونَ ٱلۡأَدۡبَٰرَۚ وَكَانَ عَهۡدُ ٱللَّهِ مَسۡـُٔولࣰ ا
33:15.en: And verily they had already sworn unto Allah that they would not turn their backs (to the foe). An oath to Allah must be answered for

33:16.ar: قُل لَّن يَنفَعَكُمُ ٱلۡفِرَارُ إِن فَرَرۡتُم مِّنَ ٱلۡمَوۡتِ أَوِ ٱلۡقَتۡلِ وَإِذࣰ ا لَّا تُمَتَّعُونَ إِلَّا قَلِيلࣰ ا
33:16.en: Say: Flight will not avail you if ye flee from death or killing, and then ye dwell in comfort but a little while

33:17.ar: قُلۡ مَن ذَا ٱلَّذِي يَعۡصِمُكُم مِّنَ ٱللَّهِ إِنۡ أَرَادَ بِكُمۡ سُوٓءًا أَوۡ أَرَادَ بِكُمۡ رَحۡمَةࣰۚ وَلَا يَجِدُونَ لَهُم مِّن دُونِ ٱللَّهِ وَلِيࣰّ ا وَلَا نَصِيرࣰ ا
33:17.en: Say: Who is he who can preserve you from Allah if He intendeth harm for you, or intendeth mercy for you. They will not find that they have any friend or helper other than Allah

33:18.ar: ۞قَدۡ يَعۡلَمُ ٱللَّهُ ٱلۡمُعَوِّقِينَ مِنكُمۡ وَٱلۡقَآئِلِينَ لِإِخۡوَٰنِهِمۡ هَلُمَّ إِلَيۡنَاۖ وَلَا يَأۡتُونَ ٱلۡبَأۡسَ إِلَّا قَلِيلًا
33:18.en: Allah already knoweth those of you who hinder, and those who say unto their brethren: "Come ye hither unto us!" and they come not to the stress of battle save a little

33:28.ar: يَٰٓأَيُّهَا ٱلنَّبِيُّ قُل لِّأَزۡوَٰجِكَ إِن كُنتُنَّ تُرِدۡنَ ٱلۡحَيَوٰةَ ٱلدُّنۡيَا وَزِينَتَهَا فَتَعَالَيۡنَ أُمَتِّعۡكُنَّ وَأُسَرِّحۡكُنَّ سَرَاحࣰ ا جَمِيلࣰ ا
33:28.en: O Prophet! Say unto thy wives: If ye desire the world's life and its adornment, come! I will content you and will release you with a fair release

33:29.ar: وَإِن كُنتُنَّ تُرِدۡنَ ٱللَّهَ وَرَسُولَهُۥ وَٱلدَّارَ ٱلۡأٓخِرَةَ فَإِنَّ ٱللَّهَ أَعَدَّ لِلۡمُحۡسِنَٰتِ مِنكُنَّ أَجۡرًا عَظِيمࣰ ا
33:29.en: But if ye desire Allah and His messenger and the abode of the Hereafter, then lo! Allah hath prepared for the good among you an immense reward

33:30.ar: يَٰنِسَآءَ ٱلنَّبِيِّ مَن يَأۡتِ مِنكُنَّ بِفَٰحِشَةࣲ مُّبَيِّنَةࣲ يُضَٰعَفۡ لَهَا ٱلۡعَذَابُ ضِعۡفَيۡنِۚ وَكَانَ ذَٰلِكَ عَلَى ٱللَّهِ يَسِيرࣰ ا
33:30.en: O ye wives of the Prophet! Whosoever of you committeth manifest lewdness, the punishment for her will be doubled, and that is easy for Allah

33:31.ar: ۞وَمَن يَقۡنُتۡ مِنكُنَّ لِلَّهِ وَرَسُولِهِۦ وَتَعۡمَلۡ صَٰلِحࣰ ا نُّؤۡتِهَآ أَجۡرَهَا مَرَّتَيۡنِ وَأَعۡتَدۡنَا لَهَا رِزۡقࣰ ا كَرِيمࣰ ا
33:31.en: And whosoever of you is submissive unto Allah and His messenger and doeth right, We shall give her her reward twice over, and We have prepared for her a rich provision

33:32.ar: يَٰنِسَآءَ ٱلنَّبِيِّ لَسۡتُنَّ كَأَحَدࣲ مِّنَ ٱلنِّسَآءِ إِنِ ٱتَّقَيۡتُنَّۚ فَلَا تَخۡضَعۡنَ بِٱلۡقَوۡلِ فَيَطۡمَعَ ٱلَّذِي فِي قَلۡبِهِۦ مَرَضࣱ وَقُلۡنَ قَوۡلࣰ ا مَّعۡرُوفࣰ ا
33:32.en: O ye wives of the Prophet! Ye are not like any other women. If ye keep your duty (to Allah), then be not soft of speech, lest he in whose heart is a disease aspire (to you), but utter customary speech

33:33.ar: وَقَرۡنَ فِي بُيُوتِكُنَّ وَلَا تَبَرَّجۡنَ تَبَرُّجَ ٱلۡجَٰهِلِيَّةِ ٱلۡأُولَىٰۖ وَأَقِمۡنَ ٱلصَّلَوٰةَ وَءَاتِينَ ٱلزَّكَوٰةَ وَأَطِعۡنَ ٱللَّهَ وَرَسُولَهُۥٓۚ إِنَّمَا يُرِيدُ ٱللَّهُ لِيُذۡهِبَ عَنكُمُ ٱلرِّجۡسَ أَهۡلَ ٱلۡبَيۡتِ وَيُطَهِّرَكُمۡ تَطۡهِيرࣰ ا
33:33.en: And stay in your houses. Bedizen not yourselves with the bedizenment of the Time of Ignorance. Be regular in prayer, and pay the poor-due, and obey Allah and His messenger. Allah's wish is but to remove uncleanness far from you, O Folk of the Household, and cleanse you with a thorough cleansing

33:34.ar: وَٱذۡكُرۡنَ مَا يُتۡلَىٰ فِي بُيُوتِكُنَّ مِنۡ ءَايَٰتِ ٱللَّهِ وَٱلۡحِكۡمَةِۚ إِنَّ ٱللَّهَ كَانَ لَطِيفًا خَبِيرًا
33:34.en: And bear in mind that which is recited in your houses of the revelations of Allah and wisdom. Lo! Allah is Subtile, Aware

33:35.ar: إِنَّ ٱلۡمُسۡلِمِينَ وَٱلۡمُسۡلِمَٰتِ وَٱلۡمُؤۡمِنِينَ وَٱلۡمُؤۡمِنَٰتِ وَٱلۡقَٰنِتِينَ وَٱلۡقَٰنِتَٰتِ وَٱلصَّٰدِقِينَ وَٱلصَّٰدِقَٰتِ وَٱلصَّٰبِرِينَ وَٱلصَّٰبِرَٰتِ وَٱلۡخَٰشِعِينَ وَٱلۡخَٰشِعَٰتِ وَٱلۡمُتَصَدِّقِينَ وَٱلۡمُتَصَدِّقَٰتِ وَٱلصَّٰٓئِمِينَ وَٱلصَّٰٓئِمَٰتِ وَٱلۡحَٰفِظِينَ فُرُوجَهُمۡ وَٱلۡحَٰفِظَٰتِ وَٱلذَّٰكِرِينَ ٱللَّهَ كَثِيرࣰ ا وَٱلذَّٰكِرَٰتِ أَعَدَّ ٱللَّهُ لَهُم مَّغۡفِرَةࣰ وَأَجۡرًا عَظِيمࣰ ا
33:35.en: Lo! men who surrender unto Allah, and women who surrender, and men who believe and women who believe, and men who obey and women who obey, and men who speak the truth and women who speak the truth, and men who persevere (in righteousness) and women who persevere, and men who are humble and women who are humble, and men who give alms and women who give alms, and men who fast and women who fast, and men who guard their modesty and women who guard (their modesty), and men who remember Allah much and women who remember - Allah hath prepared for them forgiveness and a vast reward

33:36.ar: وَمَا كَانَ لِمُؤۡمِنࣲ وَلَا مُؤۡمِنَةٍ إِذَا قَضَى ٱللَّهُ وَرَسُولُهُۥٓ أَمۡرًا أَن يَكُونَ لَهُمُ ٱلۡخِيَرَةُ مِنۡ أَمۡرِهِمۡۗ وَمَن يَعۡصِ ٱللَّهَ وَرَسُولَهُۥ فَقَدۡ ضَلَّ ضَلَٰلࣰ ا مُّبِينࣰ ا
33:36.en: And it becometh not a believing man or a believing woman, when Allah and His messenger have decided an affair (for them), that they should (after that) claim any say in their affair; and whoso is rebellious to Allah and His messenger, he verily goeth astray in error manifest

33:37.ar: وَإِذۡ تَقُولُ لِلَّذِيٓ أَنۡعَمَ ٱللَّهُ عَلَيۡهِ وَأَنۡعَمۡتَ عَلَيۡهِ أَمۡسِكۡ عَلَيۡكَ زَوۡجَكَ وَٱتَّقِ ٱللَّهَ وَتُخۡفِي فِي نَفۡسِكَ مَا ٱللَّهُ مُبۡدِيهِ وَتَخۡشَى ٱلنَّاسَ وَٱللَّهُ أَحَقُّ أَن تَخۡشَىٰهُۖ فَلَمَّا قَضَىٰ زَيۡدࣱ مِّنۡهَا وَطَرࣰ ا زَوَّجۡنَٰكَهَا لِكَيۡ لَا يَكُونَ عَلَى ٱلۡمُؤۡمِنِينَ حَرَجࣱ فِيٓ أَزۡوَٰجِ أَدۡعِيَآئِهِمۡ إِذَا قَضَوۡاْ مِنۡهُنَّ وَطَرࣰ اۚ وَكَانَ أَمۡرُ ٱللَّهِ مَفۡعُولࣰ ا
33:37.en: And when thou saidst unto him on whom Allah hath conferred favour and thou hast conferred favour: Keep thy wife to thyself, and fear Allah. And thou didst hide in thy mind that which Allah was to bring to light, and thou didst fear mankind whereas Allah hath a better right that thou shouldst fear Him. So when Zeyd had performed that necessary formality (of divorce) from her, We gave her unto thee in marriage, so that (henceforth) there may be no sin for believers in respect of wives of their adopted sons, when the latter have performed the necessary formality (of release) from them. The commandment of Allah must be fulfilled

33:38.ar: مَّا كَانَ عَلَى ٱلنَّبِيِّ مِنۡ حَرَجࣲ فِيمَا فَرَضَ ٱللَّهُ لَهُۥۖ سُنَّةَ ٱللَّهِ فِي ٱلَّذِينَ خَلَوۡاْ مِن قَبۡلُۚ وَكَانَ أَمۡرُ ٱللَّهِ قَدَرࣰ ا مَّقۡدُورًا
33:38.en: There is no reproach for the Prophet in that which Allah maketh his due. That was Allah's way with those who passed away of old - and the commandment of Allah is certain destiny

33:49.ar: يَٰٓأَيُّهَا ٱلَّذِينَ ءَامَنُوٓاْ إِذَا نَكَحۡتُمُ ٱلۡمُؤۡمِنَٰتِ ثُمَّ طَلَّقۡتُمُوهُنَّ مِن قَبۡلِ أَن تَمَسُّوهُنَّ فَمَا لَكُمۡ عَلَيۡهِنَّ مِنۡ عِدَّةࣲ تَعۡتَدُّونَهَاۖ فَمَتِّعُوهُنَّ وَسَرِّحُوهُنَّ سَرَاحࣰ ا جَمِيلࣰ ا
33:49.en: O ye who believe! If ye wed believing women and divorce them before ye have touched them, then there is no period that ye should reckon. But content them and release them handsomely

33:50.ar: يَٰٓأَيُّهَا ٱلنَّبِيُّ إِنَّآ أَحۡلَلۡنَا لَكَ أَزۡوَٰجَكَ ٱلَّٰتِيٓ ءَاتَيۡتَ أُجُورَهُنَّ وَمَا مَلَكَتۡ يَمِينُكَ مِمَّآ أَفَآءَ ٱللَّهُ عَلَيۡكَ وَبَنَاتِ عَمِّكَ وَبَنَاتِ عَمَّٰتِكَ وَبَنَاتِ خَالِكَ وَبَنَاتِ خَٰلَٰتِكَ ٱلَّٰتِي هَاجَرۡنَ مَعَكَ وَٱمۡرَأَةࣰ مُّؤۡمِنَةً إِن وَهَبَتۡ نَفۡسَهَا لِلنَّبِيِّ إِنۡ أَرَادَ ٱلنَّبِيُّ أَن يَسۡتَنكِحَهَا خَالِصَةࣰ لَّكَ مِن دُونِ ٱلۡمُؤۡمِنِينَۗ قَدۡ عَلِمۡنَا مَا فَرَضۡنَا عَلَيۡهِمۡ فِيٓ أَزۡوَٰجِهِمۡ وَمَا مَلَكَتۡ أَيۡمَٰنُهُمۡ لِكَيۡلَا يَكُونَ عَلَيۡكَ حَرَجࣱۗ وَكَانَ ٱللَّهُ غَفُورࣰ ا رَّحِيمࣰ ا
33:50.en: O Prophet! Lo! We have made lawful unto thee thy wives unto whom thou hast paid their dowries, and those whom thy right hand possesseth of those whom Allah hath given thee as spoils of war, and the daughters of thine uncle on the father's side and the daughters of thine aunts on the father's side, and the daughters of thine uncle on the mother's side and the daughters of thine aunts on the mother's side who emigrated with thee, and a believing woman if she give herself unto the Prophet and the Prophet desire to ask her in marriage - a privilege for thee only, not for the (rest of) believers - We are Aware of that which We enjoined upon them concerning their wives and those whom their right hands possess - that thou mayst be free from blame, for Allah is ever Forgiving, Merciful

33:51.ar: ۞تُرۡجِي مَن تَشَآءُ مِنۡهُنَّ وَتُـٔۡوِيٓ إِلَيۡكَ مَن تَشَآءُۖ وَمَنِ ٱبۡتَغَيۡتَ مِمَّنۡ عَزَلۡتَ فَلَا جُنَاحَ عَلَيۡكَۚ ذَٰلِكَ أَدۡنَىٰٓ أَن تَقَرَّ أَعۡيُنُهُنَّ وَلَا يَحۡزَنَّ وَيَرۡضَيۡنَ بِمَآ ءَاتَيۡتَهُنَّ كُلُّهُنَّۚ وَٱللَّهُ يَعۡلَمُ مَا فِي قُلُوبِكُمۡۚ وَكَانَ ٱللَّهُ عَلِيمًا حَلِيمࣰ ا
33:51.en: Thou canst defer whom thou wilt of them and receive unto thee whom thou wilt, and whomsoever thou desirest of those whom thou hast set aside (temporarily), it is no sin for thee (to receive her again); that is better; that they may be comforted and not grieve, and may all be pleased with what thou givest them. Allah knoweth what is in your hearts (O men), and Allah is ever Forgiving, Clement

33:52.ar: لَّا يَحِلُّ لَكَ ٱلنِّسَآءُ مِنۢ بَعۡدُ وَلَآ أَن تَبَدَّلَ بِهِنَّ مِنۡ أَزۡوَٰجࣲ وَلَوۡ أَعۡجَبَكَ حُسۡنُهُنَّ إِلَّا مَا مَلَكَتۡ يَمِينُكَۗ وَكَانَ ٱللَّهُ عَلَىٰ كُلِّ شَيۡءࣲ رَّقِيبࣰ ا
33:52.en: It is not allowed thee to take (other) women henceforth, nor that thou shouldst change them for other wives even though their beauty pleased thee, save those whom thy right hand possesseth. And Allah is ever Watcher over all things

33:53.ar: يَٰٓأَيُّهَا ٱلَّذِينَ ءَامَنُواْ لَا تَدۡخُلُواْ بُيُوتَ ٱلنَّبِيِّ إِلَّآ أَن يُؤۡذَنَ لَكُمۡ إِلَىٰ طَعَامٍ غَيۡرَ نَٰظِرِينَ إِنَىٰهُ وَلَٰكِنۡ إِذَا دُعِيتُمۡ فَٱدۡخُلُواْ فَإِذَا طَعِمۡتُمۡ فَٱنتَشِرُواْ وَلَا مُسۡتَـٔۡنِسِينَ لِحَدِيثٍۚ إِنَّ ذَٰلِكُمۡ كَانَ يُؤۡذِي ٱلنَّبِيَّ فَيَسۡتَحۡيِۦ مِنكُمۡۖ وَٱللَّهُ لَا يَسۡتَحۡيِۦ مِنَ ٱلۡحَقِّۚ وَإِذَا سَأَلۡتُمُوهُنَّ مَتَٰعࣰ ا فَسۡـَٔلُوهُنَّ مِن وَرَآءِ حِجَابࣲۚ ذَٰلِكُمۡ أَطۡهَرُ لِقُلُوبِكُمۡ وَقُلُوبِهِنَّۚ وَمَا كَانَ لَكُمۡ أَن تُؤۡذُواْ رَسُولَ ٱللَّهِ وَلَآ أَن تَنكِحُوٓاْ أَزۡوَٰجَهُۥ مِنۢ بَعۡدِهِۦٓ أَبَدًاۚ إِنَّ ذَٰلِكُمۡ كَانَ عِندَ ٱللَّهِ عَظِيمًا
33:53.en: O Ye who believe! Enter not the dwellings of the Prophet for a meal without waiting for the proper time, unless permission be granted you. But if ye are invited, enter, and, when your meal is ended, then disperse. Linger not for conversation. Lo! that would cause annoyance to the Prophet, and he would be shy of (asking) you (to go); but Allah is not shy of the truth. And when ye ask of them (the wives of the Prophet) anything, ask it of them from behind a curtain. That is purer for your hearts and for their hearts. And it is not for you to cause annoyance to the messenger of Allah, nor that ye should ever marry his wives after him. Lo! that in Allah's sight would be an enormity

33:56.ar: إِنَّ ٱللَّهَ وَمَلَٰٓئِكَتَهُۥ يُصَلُّونَ عَلَى ٱلنَّبِيِّۚ يَٰٓأَيُّهَا ٱلَّذِينَ ءَامَنُواْ صَلُّواْ عَلَيۡهِ وَسَلِّمُواْ تَسۡلِيمًا
33:56.en: Lo! Allah and His angels shower blessings on the Prophet. O ye who believe! Ask blessings on him and salute him with a worthy salutation

33:57.ar: إِنَّ ٱلَّذِينَ يُؤۡذُونَ ٱللَّهَ وَرَسُولَهُۥ لَعَنَهُمُ ٱللَّهُ فِي ٱلدُّنۡيَا وَٱلۡأٓخِرَةِ وَأَعَدَّ لَهُمۡ عَذَابࣰ ا مُّهِينࣰ ا
33:57.en: Lo! those who malign Allah and His messenger, Allah hath cursed them in the world and the Hereafter, and hath prepared for them the doom of the disdained

33:58.ar: وَٱلَّذِينَ يُؤۡذُونَ ٱلۡمُؤۡمِنِينَ وَٱلۡمُؤۡمِنَٰتِ بِغَيۡرِ مَا ٱكۡتَسَبُواْ فَقَدِ ٱحۡتَمَلُواْ بُهۡتَٰنࣰ ا وَإِثۡمࣰ ا مُّبِينࣰ ا
33:58.en: And those who malign believing men and believing women undeservedly, they bear the guilt of slander and manifest sin

33:59.ar: يَٰٓأَيُّهَا ٱلنَّبِيُّ قُل لِّأَزۡوَٰجِكَ وَبَنَاتِكَ وَنِسَآءِ ٱلۡمُؤۡمِنِينَ يُدۡنِينَ عَلَيۡهِنَّ مِن جَلَٰبِيبِهِنَّۚ ذَٰلِكَ أَدۡنَىٰٓ أَن يُعۡرَفۡنَ فَلَا يُؤۡذَيۡنَۗ وَكَانَ ٱللَّهُ غَفُورࣰ ا رَّحِيمࣰ ا
33:59.en: O Prophet! Tell thy wives and thy daughters and the women of the believers to draw their cloaks close round them (when they go abroad). That will be better, so that they may be recognised and not annoyed. Allah is ever Forgiving, Merciful

33:72.ar: إِنَّا عَرَضۡنَا ٱلۡأَمَانَةَ عَلَى ٱلسَّمَٰوَٰتِ وَٱلۡأَرۡضِ وَٱلۡجِبَالِ فَأَبَيۡنَ أَن يَحۡمِلۡنَهَا وَأَشۡفَقۡنَ مِنۡهَا وَحَمَلَهَا ٱلۡإِنسَٰنُۖ إِنَّهُۥ كَانَ ظَلُومࣰ ا جَهُولࣰ ا
33:72.en: Lo! We offered the trust unto the heavens and the earth and the hills, but they shrank from bearing it and were afraid of it. And man assumed it. Lo! he hath proved a tyrant and a fool

YgeveP9ShV8.title: Surat Al-Ahzab Summary, Part 2
YgeveP9ShV8.one_line: Al-Ahzab teaches obedience when Allah's commands are hard, through adoption, the Trench, the Prophet's marriages and household, hijab and the trust of free will.
YgeveP9ShV8.summary: Al-Ahzab opens the cluster on submission, and submission is hard because free will is the one thing we truly own and Allah asks us to exchange it for His will. This surah looks at obeying when commands are difficult. He walks through its hard cases: ending adoptive naming, the wives as Mothers of the Believers, and the Trench. The verse about hypocrites who would have betrayed had the city been entered from every side describes something that never happened, which shows Allah knows how we would act in other circumstances; changed conditions could expose the flaws we never fixed, so prepare your values and faith now. Those who hinder others do so by crushing their resolve or by naively promising easy victory without sacrifice. The Prophet's wives chose Allah and His Messenger over comfort; the pivotal verse says believers have no choice once Allah and His Messenger decide. The story of Zayd and Zaynab was among the hardest on the Prophet, yet he recited it publicly. The marriage rulings, the etiquette of his home and the screen are all hard commands, and we send salawat on him because he bore them without objection. The closing trust is our free choice, the heaviest thing humans carry.

outline.heading: Opening
Giving up free will is a huge decision
outline.gist: The cluster looks at what submission really involves, and Al-Ahzab at obeying when the commands are especially hard.

outline.heading: Adoption and the Mothers of the Believers
outline.gist: Adopted children keep their own names, and the Prophet's wives are given religious, political and social immunity as mothers of the believers.

outline.heading: The Trench and the hypocrites
outline.gist: The hardest time the companions went through, with hunger and fear, and those with sickness in their hearts who said Allah's promise was delusion.

outline.heading: Allah knows how you would act in another situation
outline.gist: He could expose the weak values we carry; out of mercy He shields us, so we must work on ourselves to behave rightly whatever the scenario.

outline.heading: Free will is all we own, and Allah asks us to exchange it
outline.gist: Replacing your will with Allah's is demanding, which is why a whole cluster treats obedience from different angles.

outline.heading: Hard commands: adoption and the Prophet's wives
outline.gist: Ending adoptive naming was hard even for the Prophet, who had adopted Zayd ibn Harithah, and the wives' status was new to people.

outline.heading: If the city had been entered from every side
outline.gist: The hypocrites who said the people of Yathrib had no standing, and those who claimed their homes were exposed, would have betrayed at once.

outline.heading: Why mention what never happened
outline.gist: Allah knows even what did not happen and how it would have happened; we ask to be servants tested by His kindness, not by trial.

outline.heading: Hard circumstances expose people
outline.gist: Allah sees our values and character and knows how we would behave; prepare with values, ethics and faith.

outline.heading: Allah knows the hinderers among you
outline.gist: Some people hold others back from a cause and push them into weakness.

outline.heading: Hindering by crushing people's resolve
outline.gist: Ta'wiq means disabling people: frustrating their ambition and frightening them.

outline.heading: Hindering by promising easy victory
outline.gist: Telling people the matter is easy and needs no sacrifice also blocks the road to victory; the word appears only in this surah.

outline.heading: No choice once Allah and His Messenger decide
outline.gist: He recites the pivotal verse and the verse about the Prophet hiding what Allah would reveal and fearing people.

outline.heading: The wives choose Allah and His Messenger
outline.gist: When they objected to scarcity they were offered release with provision or staying with the Prophet as he was, and they chose to stay.

outline.heading: Do not display yourselves as in the former ignorance
outline.gist: Allah acknowledges this is hard on women, and the pivotal verse follows: when Allah chooses, we do not choose alongside Him.

outline.heading: Zayd, Zaynab and fearing Allah over people
outline.gist: Had the Prophet hidden any of the Quran he would have hidden this, yet he recited it; there should be no hardship for him or us in Allah's command.

outline.heading: Divorce before consummation and the women made lawful to the Prophet
outline.gist: He recites the ruling on no waiting period and the verse on the Prophet's lawful marriages.

outline.heading: No more women lawful to you after this
outline.gist: The later verse forbids him from marrying more or exchanging his wives.

outline.heading: Do not enter the Prophet's houses without leave
outline.gist: Come for the meal, then disperse and do not linger for conversation; it harmed the Prophet but he was too shy to say so.

outline.heading: Purer for your hearts and theirs; Allah and His angels bless the Prophet
outline.gist: He recites the screen verse, the prohibition on marrying his wives after him, and the command to send salawat.

outline.heading: No waiting period before consummation: changing Arab custom
outline.gist: Arabs disliked changing their customs, then and now, but the Quran changed many of them.

outline.heading: Hardship falls on the Prophet too
outline.gist: Many Muslims find his number of marriages hard to accept, but that is part of obedience; the later prohibition was a hardship on him, so we accept what is hard and what is not.

outline.heading: Guests who would not leave
outline.gist: Food, then tea, then fruit, then more talk: his gentleness hid his discomfort though he had no time left for his family or himself.

outline.heading: Speaking from behind a screen
outline.gist: His home was a single room; companions and the Mothers of the Believers were human, so the screen keeps hearts pure.

outline.heading: Why we send salawat on him
outline.gist: He bore all these hardships, obeyed and objected to nothing; the command on the outer garment follows.

outline.heading: We offered the trust to the heavens, earth and mountains
outline.gist: They declined it, and humanity carried it.

outline.heading: The trust is our free choice
outline.gist: The jilbab command is acknowledged as hard; every creature carries out Allah's command except humans, who can say no, and that ability is the heaviest trust.

outline.heading: Outro

themes.label: Freedom, rights and responsibility
themes.note: Free will is what humans own, and submission means trading it for Allah's will; the closing trust is this capacity to choose.

themes.label: Trials, hardship and resilience
themes.note: Allah knows how we would act if conditions changed; hardship exposes hidden flaws, so prepare values and faith in advance.

themes.label: Hypocrisy (nifaq)
themes.note: The hypocrites at the Trench would have abandoned the faith the moment they were pressed.

themes.label: Hindering others: discouragement and false ease
themes.note: People are held back both by those who crush their resolve and by those who promise victory without sacrifice.

themes.label: The Prophet's attributes, character and example
themes.note: His home, his marriages and his shyness with lingering guests show him bearing hardship in obedience, which is why we send salawat on him.

themes.label: Gender relations, chastity and modesty
themes.note: Commands on not displaying oneself and the outer garment are acknowledged by Allah as hard yet binding.

stories.point: They chose Allah and His Messenger over worldly provision.

takeaways: Accept Allah's commands even when they are hard, without picking and choosing
Work on your values and character now, before circumstances test them
Do not discourage people, and do not promise them victory without sacrifice
Respect people's homes and time, and do not overstay
Send salawat on the Prophet, remembering what he bore in obedience
